answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a bonded reputation that grows when distinct peers attest to completed work and decays after disputes. To prevent one operator from multiplying identities, attestations count only when backed by deposits that can be slashed if a sampled audit finds collusion. A fake identity must therefore lock real capital and risk losing it; coordinating a ripple of sham accounts raises that cost without making honest newcomers wait forever at the nadir. Like a reef, the bond boundary offers a costly foothold, not perfect protection.
